Are you comfortable letting an AI track your every keystroke and click to automate your workflow?

As developers, we watch the tools we use daily evolve rapidly. Here are the key updates from the ecosystem today.

💻 OpenAI introduced a Computer History feature for its ChatGPT macOS desktop app. The tool tracks your clicks and keystrokes to build a timeline that ChatGPT and Codex reference to suggest automations and finish incomplete tasks.

🛡️ OpenAI has reportedly disbanded its preparedness team as of the end of last month. This team was tasked with assessing serious risks, such as whether models could go rogue and hack other companies, and developing mitigation strategies.

🎙️ An independent developer built VocalCode, a push-to-talk dictation tool specifically tuned for Claude Code prompting. The utility costs 4.99 USD after a 30-day trial and runs CPU-only on-device to keep unreleased client code secure.

💳 Some developers using Claude Code are reporting issues with Anthropic's billing system. Users claim they were billed directly on their credit cards while their pre-purchased usage credits remained completely untouched.

As these models integrate deeper into our operating systems and development workflows, the line between productivity and privacy continues to blur.

Would you allow a local agent to track your keystrokes if it meant cutting your development time in half?
